title: Which file goes in which loader and folder

questions.q: A file's tensor names all begin with double_blocks, single_blocks or img_in. Which loader fits?
questions.why: Those are denoiser layers with no text encoder and no VAE, so you load those separately.

questions.q: A new file doesn't show in the loader's menu. What is the first thing to check?
options: Whether it sits under the folder that loader reads, with a known extension
Whether the file is too big
questions.answer: Whether it sits under the folder that loader reads, with a known extension
questions.why: A menu is a directory listing filtered by extension. .gguf, for example, is not on the list.

questions.q: You put the same file name in models/clip and models/text_encoders. Which one loads?
options: The one in text_encoders, because that folder is listed first
questions.answer: The one in text_encoders, because that folder is listed first
questions.why: get_full_path returns the first match in folder order. The menu shows just one entry, so you can't tell from the menu.

questions.q: What does moving a checkpoint from models/checkpoints to models/diffusion_models change?
options: Which menu lists it, and nothing about the file
questions.answer: Which menu lists it, and nothing about the file
questions.why: The folder only decides which menu shows it. The file is the same bytes. UNETLoader would then take just the denoiser out.

questions.q: A graph uses Load Checkpoint with a denoiser-only file, and CLIPTextEncode fails with clip input is invalid: None. Why?
options: The file has no text encoder, so the CLIP output is empty
The CLIP model is the wrong family
questions.answer: The file has no text encoder, so the CLIP output is empty
questions.why: The loader warns and tries it as a diffusion model, then returns None for CLIP. Load the text encoder and VAE with their own loaders.
